result:
I found 11 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings (or the shared rules in the module docstring), and fixed all of them. I checked all 150 rules by turning each docstring into a reference calculation and comparing results across a grid of quantities and unit prices. After the fixes, all 150 match and negative inputs still raise `ValueError`.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 19, 40 | The threshold was `qty >= 11`, but the docstring says 10+ units | Changed to `qty >= 10` |
| 21, 52, 144 | The price was capped and then discounted (`min(base, 30000) * pct // 100`), but the shared rules say the cap applies to the discount | Discount is now `base * pct // 100`, then `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 51, 53 | Rounded with `round(base * pct / 100)`, but the shared rules say discounts are rounded down to the won | Changed to `base * pct // 100` |
| 74 | Calculated as marginal (only units above the threshold), but the docstring says whole | Changed to `base * 12 // 100` |
| 118 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000, so discounts between 30,001 and 60,000 weren't capped | Always applies `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 136, 145 | Calculated as whole, but the docstring says marginal | Changed to `(qty - threshold) * unit * pct // 100` |

Some rules are written differently from the rest, such as `N <= qty`, `not qty < N`, `if disc > N: disc = N`, and `(qty * unit) * …` (rules 13, 27, 31, 42, 43, 54 and others). They behave the same as the docstring, so I left them as they were.

STATUS: DONE
